predecessors.name: Sultanate of Johor
predecessors.text: the Dutch-controlled southern part of the Johor-Riau sultanate, divided by the Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1824

successors.name: Dutch East Indies
successors.text: the Riau Archipelago, under direct Dutch rule from 1913

ledger.x: 1824: the Dutch half of Johor-Riau becomes the Riau-Lingga Sultanate, seat Daik on Lingga.
1824: the southern, Dutch-sphere half of the Johor-Riau sultanate passes to the new Riau-Lingga Sultanate.
1824: the sultanate is a Dutch protectorate from its foundation.
1857: the Dutch depose Sultan Mahmud IV; Sulaiman Badrul Alam Shah II is sultan from that year and the sultanate continues.
1900: the royal seat moves from Daik to Tanjung Pinang.
11 February 1911: the protectorate ends when the Dutch abolish the sultanate ('Abolished by the Dutch: 11 February 1911'; 'The Dutch officially annexed the sultanate').
1911: the Dutch abolish the Riau-Lingga Sultanate.

certainty.note: The sphere line south of the Strait of Singapore was fixed by the Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1824 (the page says that line later became the Indonesia-Malaysia border); the Indragiri mainland enclaves are approximate.
